articles.title: Functional Outcomes of Pediatrics and Adolescent Pelvic Fractures: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Buckman V, Sun P, Blibo J, Pandya N
articles.study_type: Systematic review of retrospective and prospective cohort studies and case series
articles.population: Children and adolescents with pelvic fractures
articles.outcomes: Functional outcomes including independent ambulation and return to daily activities; structural complications such as pelvic asymmetry, limb length discrepancy, acetabular dysplasia, and nonunion
articles.take_home: Most children and young people with pelvic fractures (over 90%) regain the ability to walk independently and return to normal daily activities regardless of how they are treated. Serious complications are uncommon, though pelvic asymmetry occurs in about 9% of cases.

articles.title: Pediatric Musculoskeletal Radiograph Interpretation Among Orthopaedic Surgery Postgraduate Trainees: A Competency-Based Education Intervention.
articles.authors: Starvaggi CA, Bouchard M, Camp M, Carsen S, Mortimer AJ, Katchky R, et al.
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy improved by 10.5%, localization accuracy by 11.9%, and risk stratification accuracy by 20.5%. 78% of trainees successfully reached the 90% performance standard. 84.6% of survey respondents supported integrating the intervention into residency training.
articles.take_home: A web-based training programme with immediate feedback substantially improved trainee doctors' ability to detect fractures, locate injuries and assess risk severity on children's x-rays. Most trainees found the approach helpful and thought it should be part of standard orthopaedic training.

articles.title: The Role of Caudal Screw Fixation in Outcomes of Posterior Dynamic Distracting Device for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.
articles.authors: Rogie GA, Braithwaite Iv H, Luhmann S
articles.population: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients treated with posterior dynamic distracting device
articles.sample_size: 155 patients, mean age 14.4 years, mean follow-up 2.3 years
articles.outcomes: Curve correction, construct breakage, mechanical failure rates, and revision surgery rates. Initial curve improved from 46 degrees to 21 degrees. Construct breakage occurred in 17%, overall mechanical failure in 27%, and revisions for mechanical failure in 14%.
articles.take_home: The posterior dynamic distracting device successfully corrected scoliosis curves, but mechanical failure occurred in about one in four patients. The angle at which the bottom screw was positioned was more important than its depth or size in preventing complications and the need for further surgery.

articles.title: Radiographic Anomalies of the Tarsal Navicular.
articles.authors: Abraham VM, Marletta D, De Salvo S, Hartman R, Chang J, Zide J, et al.
articles.population: Children presenting to a paediatric hospital for foot radiographs
articles.outcomes: Prevalence and characterisation of tarsal navicular abnormalities; types identified included dorsal avulsion, ossification, bossing, avascular necrosis, osteochondritis dissecans, spurring and accessory bones
articles.take_home: About 3% of children's foot X-rays show navicular bone abnormalities, but most of these findings are not causing the child's pain or symptoms. Doctors should be aware these incidental findings exist so they can focus treatment on what is actually causing the problem.

articles.title: Thermal Risk During Bivalving of Fiberglass Casts Following Orthopaedic Reduction: A Comparative Analysis of 2 Commercially Available Cast Padding Products.
articles.authors: Donnelley CA, Reuter A, Donnelley JE, Noback PC, Tommasini S, Luo X
articles.population: Custom upper-extremity cast model with thermal probes (not human subjects)
articles.outcomes: Temperature change during cast bivalving; maximum temperatures relative to burn injury thresholds of 44 degrees Celsius
articles.take_home: Both types of cast padding tested allowed temperatures to rise significantly during cast removal, with some runs exceeding burn thresholds in both groups. Webril padding offered slightly better protection than Specialist padding, but neither provided consistently adequate thermal protection to prevent potential burns during the procedure.

articles.title: Association Between Idiopathic Clubfoot and Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip: Do We Need Universal Screening for It?
articles.authors: Krespi R, Gigi R, Hemo Y, Danino B, Ovadia D
articles.study_type: Retrospective review of prospectively collected data
articles.population: Infants with idiopathic clubfoot treated at a single tertiary paediatric orthopaedic centre
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) identified by hip ultrasonography at 6 weeks of age using Graf classification
articles.take_home: DDH was found in only 0.78% of infants with idiopathic clubfoot, which is comparable to the general population rate, suggesting that clubfoot alone is not a reason for routine hip screening in selective screening systems. All cases of DDH identified were successfully treated alongside clubfoot treatment without complications.
